card.situation:
DHA PAE MDS AWACS solicitation seeking a unified Application, Workflow, Adoption, and Change Support services contractor across EUS Pillars 2, 3, and 5 for 11 clinical user domains, integrating with ServiceNow, JKO, MED365, and MHS GENESIS from Day 1 with 24/7 global hospital coverage.
Reached the owner because NAICS 541512 matches, the solicitation is unrestricted, and the firm holds Secret-cleared staff and ITIL 4/cybersecurity credentials that partially align to the IT infrastructure layer of the requirement.
reasons_for: 22 Secret-cleared staff satisfy the Day-1 SECRET clearance mandate for trainers and DDIL-deploying personnel, removing a common disqualifier [5ad10c73-af9cb6ff-p10-48f98b1c].

ITIL 4 certification and Army CoE help desk past performance provide a credible foundation for the ITSM/ServiceNow integration layer of Pillar 1 pass-through requirements [5ad10c73-af9cb6ff-p3-f19b5676].
CMMC Level 2 self-assessment and NIST SP 800-171 implementation satisfy the cybersecurity baseline and Basic Assessment obligation required at contract award [5ad10c73-09f81d19-p5-5742f01d].
reasons_against: Zero clinical informatics, MHS GENESIS, or health IT experience exists in the profile, leaving the core scope of Pillars 2, 3, and 5 entirely unaddressed and the Section 1 whitepaper uncreditable [5ad10c73-af9cb6ff-p8-b3ed3b78].

No training design, adoption, change management, JKO LMS, or multimodal training delivery capability is stated, creating decisive gaps across Pillars 3 and 5 and the Day-1 continuity crosswalk [5ad10c73-425abe19-p1-01eafd57; 5ad10c73-425abe19-p1-4ba04d8a].

Firm revenue (~$4.5M total past performance) and a single domestic NOC cannot credibly support 24/7 global hospital operations or enterprise-scale Day-1 consolidation of an incumbent multi-pillar health IT program [5ad10c73-425abe19-p1-976b6a8d; 5ad10c73-425abe19-p1-697eff21].

drafts.capability_statement:
Sooner Systems LLC is a NAICS 541512 information technology firm with a demonstrated record of delivering end-user IT services to federal defense customers. Our relevant experience includes a Tier 1/Tier 2 help desk and desktop support contract for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Tulsa District (2022–2025), and a systems administration and Microsoft 365/Azure migration engagement for the Oklahoma National Guard (2023–2025).

We maintain 22 personnel holding active Secret clearances, satisfying the Day-1 SECRET clearance requirement for personnel supporting application training and DDIL-environment deployments. Our bench holds ITIL 4 certifications and Security+ credentials across technical staff, supporting DoDM 8140.03 IA role compliance and ITSM-aligned service delivery. We operate a 24×7 Network Operations Center in Norman, Oklahoma, enabling continuous monitoring and sub-one-hour US-CERT incident reporting.

Our cybersecurity posture includes a CMMC Level 2 self-assessment grounded in NIST SP 800-171, RMF/ATO documentation experience, and Microsoft Azure administration on a FedRAMP Moderate-authorized platform.

We recognize that the AWACS scope — spanning clinical application workflow support, health IT adoption, change management, and global hospital operations — extends significantly beyond our current profile. We are evaluating teaming arrangements with health IT and clinical informatics partners to address Pillars 2, 3, and 5 capability gaps before determining whether to submit a Phase 1 whitepaper.

Point of Contact: [Owner Name], [Title], Sooner Systems LLC | [email] | [phone]
questions_for_co: Clinical Informaticist Minimum Qualifications [5ad10c73-425abe19-p1-1f2c6b41]: The solicitation requires offerors to propose and justify minimum qualifications for clinical informaticists — will the Government provide a minimum qualification baseline or acceptable credential equivalency list (e.g., CPHIMS, RN with informatics experience, AMIA certification) to guide offeror proposals, or is qualification determination entirely at offeror discretion?

Day-1 Consolidation Scope and Incumbent Transition Data [5ad10c73-425abe19-p1-697eff21]: The Government confirmed that all existing activities must be fully consolidated under the AWACS operating model on Day 1 — will a sanitized workload-to-capacity baseline or incumbent staffing model be released prior to proposal submission to allow offerors to right-size their Day-1 transition plans?

JKO Access and CBT Ownership [5ad10c73-425abe19-p1-4ba04d8a]: The solicitation states JKO is the Government LMS and hosts existing CBTs — will the contractor be granted JKO author/administrator access to update or create content, or is the contractor's role limited to tracking and reporting against Government-owned CBT content?

CEPO Compliance Applicability [5ad10c73-425abe19-p1-5ae6f094]: The requirement to maintain 100% compliance with Continuing Education Program Office (CEPO) standards applies to training delivery — does CEPO compliance apply to all contractor-delivered training across all 11 User Domains, or only to clinical continuing education activities, and will the Government provide the current CEPO standards document as a reference attachment?

HIPAA, Privacy Act, and 42 CFR Part 2 Staff Training Mechanism [5ad10c73-09f81d19-p10-1cfa14a9]: The solicitation requires all contractor staff to receive training on the Privacy Act, HIPAA, and 42 CFR Part 2 — will the Government provide or designate an approved training course (e.g., via JKO or DHA learning portal), or is the contractor responsible for developing and delivering a compliant training program independently?

DSA and DUA Determination Timeline [5ad10c73-09f81d19-p10-932a4f3e]: The solicitation requires the contractor to consult with the DHA Privacy Office to determine whether a Data Sharing Agreement or Data Use Agreement is required — will this determination occur pre-award, allowing offerors to account for it in their technical approach, or is it a post-award administrative action?

reader.scope_summary: DHA PAE MDS is acquiring Application, Workflow, Adoption, and Change Support (AWACS) services focused on transforming and integrating EUS Service Pillars 2 (Application & Clinical Workflow Support), 3 (Enablement & Adoption Services), and 5 (Change, Communications, & Trust) across 11 distinct User Domains ranging from point-of-care clinicians to operational combat medics. The contractor must deliver an outcome-based, unified service model integrating with Government-provided platforms (ServiceNow, JKO, MED365, MHS GENESIS) from Day 1, maintaining 24/7 support for global hospital operations, and feeding data to the enterprise ITSM and SIAM. The anticipated contract structure is a 12-month base plus four 12-month options, awarded as either a FAR-based contract or a Prototype Project Other Transaction Agreement under 10 U.S.C. § 4022, leveraging the DHA Enterprise-Wide Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) HT003826SC005.
reader.evaluation_basis: Phase 1 whitepapers must be organized into three sections: Section 1 (Innovation and Technical Strategy for Pillars 2, 3, & 5), Section 2 (Proposed Performance Outcomes including SLAs and XLAs), and a mandatory Appendix A Day 1 Continuity Crosswalk; the AOI references evaluation of "Innovation and Modernization Value" and requires ATO or ATO-C by contract award, but a detailed weighting or factor-by-factor evaluation scheme is not stated.
reader.incumbent_or_history: The Q&A references "existing activities" currently dispersed across teams and asks whether consolidation must occur on Day 1, and the Government confirmed "Government expect those existing activities to be fully consolidated under a unified AWACS operating model on Day 1"; one Q&A entry asks "If incumbent-specific information cannot be released, will the Government provide a sanitized workload-to-capacity baseline" — indicating an incumbent exists but no incumbent name or prior award details are disclosed in the text.
